column1: # Live RBAC route matrix: Phase 4 (sharing, read-only). Each step adds the rows of the behaviour it
# changes; a row of an earlier file whose answer a step changes is tagged superseded-by:p4 there.
# Columns: id, since, actor, method, path, body, expect, tags (see tests/rbac_matrix_live.sh).
# A row that needs a share or sharing in force is tagged sharing:on and SKIPs while
# RBAC_SHARING_ENABLED reads off. Run with the switch on and the instance policy enabled (sharing_policy.enabled by SQL
# on the shared instance), after step 4.4, whose seed (webapp/scripts/e2e-rbac-seed.mjs) provides:
#   viewer      a member account (rbac-viewer@e2e.local) holding a Read share, without Raw data,
#   PSHARED_ID  a project owned by member_c, never PA (baseline rows expect member_b to get 404 on
#               PA), whose cypherfixGithubToken, graphqlAuthValue and one httpxCustomHeaders entry
# ---- step 4.1: owner secrets withheld from every non-owner read ----
# The owner row proves the fake secret is really on the row, so the viewer's lacks= is not vacuous.
# The RoE downloads refuse a non-owner before any lookup (OQ-53), so no document needs seeding: the
# owner reaches the lookup (404, nothing uploaded), the viewer gets owner_only for both downloads,
# and the revision list (metadata) stays a read.
# ---- step 4.3: projectAccess() with shares, oversight; my-access; the terminal stays the owner's ----
# p4-myaccess-other needs no share and runs in either switch state. With RBAC_SHARING_ENABLED off
# /my-access does not exist (404, the owner too) and the project GET carries no myAccess (DV-30):
# the two *-off rows; the owner's my-access answer is a sharing:on row. With sharing in force admin_a
# (Full admin, projects:oversee) reads rbac-PA at Read without Raw data: the twelve admin_a rows of
# baseline.tsv are tagged sharing:off, and these are their answers for the routes whose oversight
# answer is settled; the graph, conversation, remediation, report, schedule, triage and recon status
# rows come with the read waves (4.6-4.8) and 4.14.
# ---- step 4.4: share, change, revoke and leave ----
# member_c shares PSHARED (the seed's Read shares: viewer, viewer_raw with Raw data, viewer_tmp). Refusals are
# built to write nothing: an unknown email, oneself, a write level and an existing share are refused before or
# without a change (each counted lookup is audited). viewer_tmp's share is then revoked (its next read is 404, a
# second revoke 404), granted again (the answer names the recipient, D-24) and left (its next read 404, a second
# leave 404); the next seed puts it back. The note PATCH is rewritten by the next seed too.
# With sharing off the share routes do not exist (DV-30).
# ---- step 4.8: the Priority Board and remediations at Read ----
# The viewer reads PSHARED's board, muted list, mute rules and remediations, from member_c's graph and
# rows (the seed puts no finding or remediation there, so the answers are empty), and every triage
# and remediation write answers 403 naming its permission. The remediation write probe also names a
# column that does not exist, so a guard that let it through would fail in Prisma (500), never create
# a row; the verdict and mute probes carry no node, so nothing is written past the guard either.
# admin_a reads rbac-PA by oversight: the sharing:on answers of bl-triage-list-admin and
# ---- step 4.7: collaborator reads, wave B: recon, reports, versions, RoE, auth profile, schedules ----
# A read share reads recon status (the logs are an event stream: unit-tested only), the RoE read view (OQ-53:
# metadata and the enforced scope, never the contacts, text or document), the auth profile's metadata, the recording
# status, the schedules and the run history.
# The six scan-result downloads and the AI attack-surface transcript are raw outputs: recon:read plus Raw data & files
# (requireLevel R*), so the viewer gets 403 naming recon:read and R*, viewer_raw reaches the route (nothing was
# scanned on PSHARED: the lookup's 404), the owner likewise. One row per permission and write level for the viewer
# and the overseer is generated: p4_generated.tsv. The oversight rows of the reports, schedules and recon status
# routes (admin_a on rbac-PA) answer baseline's sharing:off admin_a rows.
# ---- step 4.6: collaborator reads, wave A: graph, Insights, attack chains, text-to-cypher ----
# The viewer reads the owner's graph and Insights of PSHARED (every graph read filters on the project, never the
# caller); every graph write and the NL generator (agent:assistants, a write level that spends a key) answer 403.
# The owner rows keep the viewer's 200s from being vacuous. admin_a (projects:oversee) reads rbac-PA the same way:
# these are the graph answers of baseline's sharing:off admin_a rows. Identical node counts for owner, viewer and
# overseer (RM:p4-graph-counts) need seeded graph nodes: tests/rbac_graph_counts_live.sh.
